library(dplyr)
library(heatmaply)
library(htmlwidgets)
library(webshot2)

docker_save_pdf <- function(widget, filename, width = 950, height = 900) {
  Sys.setenv(CHROMOTE_CHROME_ARGS = "--headless --no-sandbox --disable-dev-shm-usage --disable-gpu")
  temp_h <- tempfile(fileext = ".html")
  htmlwidgets::saveWidget(widget, temp_h, selfcontained = TRUE)
  webshot2::webshot(url = temp_h, file = filename, vwidth = width, vheight = height)
  unlink(temp_h) # Clean up the temp html
}


log_info('Heatmap Visual for proteins ...')

selected <- data$toptable %>% filter(differential_expressed %in% c('UP','DOWN'))  %>% pull(Uniprot_id)

#app <- as.data.frame(colData(pe)) %>% filter( Group %in% sample_rel)%>% arrange(Group) %>% dplyr::select(- SampleName)  
# sample_rel
ordered_sample <- as.data.frame(colData(pe)) %>%
  # Force row names into a dedicated column if Sample_Number isn't explicitly there
  tibble::rownames_to_column(var = "Sample_") %>% 
  
  # Filter to retain ONLY the samples relevant to the current comparison loop
  # (Assuming sample_rel contains the target sample IDs for this specific contrast)
  filter(Sample_ %in% sample_rel) %>% 
  
  # Group blocks together perfectly
  arrange(Group) %>% pull(Sample_)


data <-  assay(pe[["proteinRS"]])[selected,ordered_sample,drop = FALSE]

log_info(dim(data)[1])
log_info(dim(data)[2])
if (dim(data)[1] > 5) {
  #   if (dim(data)[1] >= 50 & dim(data)[2] < 25){
  #     w <- 800
  #     h <- 1200
  # }else{
  #     w <- 800
  #     h <-  700
  # }
  
  #log_info('Plotting HEatmap')
  #log_info("{paste(dim(data), collapse = '\n')}")
  
  # heatmaply::heatmaply(data, scale = "none" , 
  #                 dendrogram =  "none", width = 1000 , height =900 , 
  #                 widget_id = paste0("heatmap_", sample.int(1e6, 1)),
  #                 file =  file.path(path,paste0("Heatmap_DE_proteins",".pdf")), 
  #                 cexRow = 1 )
  
clean_matrix <- na.omit(data)

# Step B: Remove rows containing ANY missing values (na.omit)
clean_matrix <- na.omit(clean_matrix)

# Step C: Remove zero-variance rows (Clustering will fail if a row has 0 variance)
if (nrow(clean_matrix) > 0) {
  row_vars <- apply(clean_matrix, 1, var, na.rm = TRUE)
  clean_matrix <- clean_matrix[row_vars > 0 & !is.na(row_vars), , drop = FALSE]
}

# Final check: Do we still have rows left after stripping all NAs?
n_rows <- nrow(clean_matrix)
n_cols <- ncol(clean_matrix)

#if (n_rows > 5) { # Needs at least a few rows to cluster meaningfully
  
  # Dynamically scale font size
  col_font_size <- max(7.5, min(11, 140 / n_cols)) 
  row_font_size <- max(8.5, min(12, 100 / n_rows))

  # Establish explicit pixel dimensions (adding extra width space for the dendrogram tree)
  calc_width  <- max(1000, n_cols * 15 + 300)
  calc_height <- max(600, n_rows * 16 + 180)

  # Truncate row names safely
  rownames(clean_matrix) <- rownames(clean_matrix) %>%
    stringr::str_replace_all(";.*", " (+)") %>%
    stringr::str_trunc(width = 20, side = "right")

  # ==============================================================================
  # 2. Build the Heatmap with Row Clustering
  # ==============================================================================
  p <- heatmaply::heatmaply(
    clean_matrix,
    scale = "row",
    dendrogram = "row",   
    Rowv = TRUE,          
    Colv = FALSE,         
    plot_method = "plotly", 
    
    # LOCK DIMENSIONS: Forces the browser to respect dimensions instead of guessing
    width = 1000,         
    height = 750,        
    
    # HARDCODE LAYOUT RATIO: Dedicates 80% width to heatmap, 20% to dendrogram tree
    subplot_widths = c(0.80, 0.20),
    
    widget_id = paste0("heatmap_", sample.int(1e6, 1)),
    colors = viridis::viridis(n = 256, option = "viridis"),
    na.value = "#EAEAEA",
    grid_gap = 0.5,
    grid_color = "#FFFFFF",
    
    fontsize_row = row_font_size,
    fontsize_col = col_font_size,
    column_text_angle = 45,       
    
    margins = c(80, 120, 30, 30), 
    show_labels = TRUE   
  )

  # Save your pristine PDF copy
  #docker_save_pdf(p, file.path(path, paste0("Heatmap_DE_proteins", ".pdf")))

  # ==============================================================================
  # 3. Direct Native Render (No layout-breaking `div` wrapper)
  # ==============================================================================
  knitr::knit_print(p) 

    } else {
    cat ('Not enough DE proteins for heatmap visualization')
  }
